newsitem.title: UK: One wounded as British police foil IRA attack.
newsitem.headline: One wounded as British police foil IRA attack.

text.p: British police said on Monday they had foiled a possible major IRA attack on the British mainland with the arrest of six men and the seizure of a large quantity of explosives.

Britain's Press Association news agency said one of the arrested men was wounded in a shoot-out with police in a west London area. He was believed to be in a serious condition but no one else was hurt, said the agency.
The swoop by anti-terrorist and special branch police officers took place early on Monday in London and another area of southern England.

"A very large quantity of explosives was recovered, as well as firearms and bomb-making equipment," said a police statement. "The operation has undoubtedly frustrated a serious imminent IRA (Irish Republican Army) terrorist attack on the British mainland involving the deployment of a large vehicle bomb likely to have caused grave loss of life and massive disruption."
The IRA launched a number of bombings on the British mainland earlier this year after ending a ceasefire because it said it was frustrated with the progress of peace efforts in Northern Ireland.
No other details were immediately available.
